---
title: "Pairwise posterior direction probabilities"
subtitle: "1.8 · the direction probability of two independent normal posteriors, after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024)"
description: "Direction probabilities from the difference of two independent normal posterior variables."
---

For two units A and B, $\pi_{AB} = \Pr(\theta_A > \theta_B \mid Y)$ is the posterior probability that A's true value exceeds B's—the area above zero under the posterior of A − B.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Means .30 and .10, SDs .20 and .20.** $\pi_{AB}$ = .760; difference SD .283 (.707 SDs above).
- **Means .30 and .10, SDs .20 and .60.** Difference widens to SD .632 (.316 SDs above), lowering $\pi_{AB}$ to .624.
- **Means .20 and .20, SDs .20 and .40.** Equal means give $\pi_{AB}$ = .500 (difference SD .447).
- **Means 1.20 and .95, SDs .20 and .20.** Tutorial sites A and B give $\pi_{AB}$ = .812.

```{=html}
<details>
<summary>Model assumptions and source notes</summary>
<p>Under independent normal posteriors with positive SDs, the larger mean always gives &pi; &gt; .5 and &pi;<sub>BA</sub> = 1 &minus; &pi;<sub>AB</sub> because equality has probability zero. Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), section II.E, Example 1, and slide 27 use the special case with both SDs equal to 1.</p>
</details>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}

```r
library(postrank)
1 - pr_tutorial$one$e["A", "B", "score_A"]   # 0.8116204: tutorial sites A and B, one minus the stored error
pnorm((1.20 - .95) / sqrt(.20^2 + .20^2))    # 0.8116204: the app's formula at the same means and SDs
```
